patients.summary: Elementary school teacher with type 2 diabetes who joins in 2019, is diagnosed with asthma and reflux by pulmonology, has three pregnancies complicated by postpartum hyponatremic seizure, placenta accreta and epidural hypotension, and is admitted to an ICU for status asthmaticus after her last practice visit.

events.reason: New patient, transfer of diabetes care

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34 y/o woman establishing care. Moved her care here because her old office kept losing her messages. Teaches second grade.

Type 2 diabetes found on routine labs in spring 2017 at her prior practice. Started metformin then and has been on 1000 mg twice a day for about two years, tolerating it apart from loose stools in the first month. Does not check sugars at home most weeks. No eye exam in over a year.

OB/GYN: one pregnancy, a missed miscarriage in 2018 that needed a D&C. Sees her own gynecologist for Paps; last one normal per patient.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID.
Allergies: none to medicines.
Family: mother has asthma, and had preeclampsia with one of her pregnancies. Father has type 2 diabetes.
Social: married. Never a smoker. A glass of wine at the occasional dinner out.

ROS: no polyuria or polydipsia, no vision change, no numbness in the feet. Otherwise negative.

Exam: well, pleasant. Vitals per flowsheet. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen soft, nontender. Feet: skin intact, no calluses, monofilament felt at all sites, DP pulses 2+ both sides.

Assessment and plan:
1. Type 2 diabetes. Continue metformin at current dose. A1c, CMP, lipids, CBC, urine microalbumin today. Eye exam referral to optometry. Hep B series recommended for diabetes, first dose at next visit.
2. Health maintenance: one-time HCV and HIV screening today, she agrees. Pap with her gynecologist. PHQ-2 negative.
3. Will request records from prior office.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Daisy, your bloodwork is back. A1c is 6.4, which is right where we want it. Kidney and liver tests, blood counts and cholesterol are all fine. The urine protein test was normal, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Let's keep metformin the same and recheck in November.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records from patient's previous primary care office, 38 pages, filed. Summary for PCP: type 2 diabetes diagnosed April 2017, metformin titrated to 1000 mg twice daily by fall 2017. Gynecology note from 2018 documents a first-trimester missed abortion managed with D&C, uncomplicated. Cervical cytology 2018 negative per gyn letter. No other chronic problems listed.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed prior office records. Nothing that changes the plan. Diabetes history matches what she told me.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM
Immunization administration

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
DM f/u. Feeling fine. Busy term at school, eating more takeout than she'd like. Taking metformin both doses most days, misses the evening one maybe once a week. Saw optometry in October, letter pending.

Exam: comfortable. Lungs clear, heart regular. No foot lesions.

Plan: A1c today. Flu vaccine given. Hep B dose 1 of 2 given, second in a month with the nurse. Encouraged a pill box for the evening dose. Back in 3 months for her physical.

documents.title: Vaccine administration
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Heplisav-B 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. VIS given for both. Tolerated, no reaction before leaving.

procedures.procedure: Immunization administration

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In before school for second Heplisav-B dose. No problems after the first. Given IM left deltoid. Series complete; updated immunization record.

procedures.procedure: Preventive visit, established patient, 18-39

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Here fasting.

Interval: no illnesses. Diet has slipped over the winter. Walking less since it got dark early. Optometry letter from October still not in our chart; she thinks it was normal.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID. NKDA.
PHQ-2: 1.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals reviewed. Eyes: no injection. Oropharynx clear. Neck no nodes, thyroid normal. Heart: regular, S1 S2, no murmur. Lungs: clear bilaterally, good air movement. Abdomen soft, no masses. Skin: no acanthosis. Feet: monofilament normal both sides, no ulcers, pulses good.

A/P
- T2DM: A1c, BMP, lipids, urine microalbumin. If A1c is creeping up, we'll talk diet before adding anything.
- Pap with her GYN, due 2021.
- Contraception per GYN, none currently; they would like another child at some point. Discussed planning ahead for pregnancy with diabetes and seeing OB early.
- Immunizations: flu and hep B done this season.

RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c higher at 7.6. Lipids and kidney function fine, urine microalbumin normal. Sent her a note: more walking and cut back on sweet drinks; recheck in early summer.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: metformin 1000 mg, asking for 90-day supply with 3 refills. Pended for PCP. Approved and sent.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from her kitchen; she confirmed her name and birth date. Teaching remotely since March, which she says has been exhausting. Has been cooking at home more and walking the neighborhood after dinner. No home glucose log but feels fine. No new symptoms. Taking metformin.

No exam today beyond appearance: looks well, speaking full sentences, no distress.

Plan: A1c at the lab this week (order placed). Continue metformin. In-person visit in the fall with flu shot.

documents.title: A1c result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c improved. Message to patient: nice work, the walks are paying off. Same plan.

documents.title: Optometry report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated eye examination, performed 2020-08-04. Indication: diabetes mellitus. Visual acuity 20/20 each eye with correction. Anterior segments quiet. Dilated fundus exam: discs sharp, vessels normal caliber, no hemorrhages, exudates or microaneurysms either eye. Impression: no diabetic retinopathy. Return in 12 months. Copy to primary care.

orders.reason: episodic wheeze and chest tightness, evaluate for asthma

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in after school. Since about June, spells of feeling short of breath with a tight chest and a whistle when she breathes out. Worse at night, sometimes wakes her around 2 or 3 am. Also brought on by brisk walking up the hill near her house. Spells settle on their own in 20 to 30 minutes. No fever, no sputum, no leg swelling, no chest pain with exertion apart from the tightness. Never smoked. No pets. Mom has asthma.

Exam: no distress, talking easily. Vitals as charted, sat normal on room air. Lungs clear today, no wheeze even with forced exhalation. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. Episodic wheeze, nocturnal and exertional, strong family history: suspect asthma. Albuterol MDI with spacer, 2 puffs as needed; technique reviewed with the MA. Referral to pulmonology for spirometry and challenge testing if needed. Asked her to keep a short diary of when it happens.
2. DM: A1c and BMP today.
3. Flu shot today.

Call sooner if she is using the inhaler more than a couple of times a week or it's not helping.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c stable, BMP normal. No changes.

events.reason: Episodic shortness of breath, chest tightness and wheeze

medications.drug_text: fluticasone propionate 0.1 MG/ACTUAT / salmeterol 0.05 MG/ACTUAT Dry Powder Inhaler
medications.sig: Inhale 1 puff twice daily; rinse mouth after use

reports.text: Pre-bronchodilator spirometry with acceptable and repeatable efforts. FEV1 2.8 L (80% predicted). FVC 3.5 L (85% predicted). FEV1/FVC 0.80. Flow-volume loop of normal contour. Methacholine bronchoprovocation performed per protocol after withholding bronchodilator: FEV1 fell 20% from baseline at a methacholine concentration of 8 mg/mL. Recovered with albuterol.
reports.conclusion: Normal baseline spirometry. Positive methacholine challenge at 8 mg/mL, supporting airway hyperresponsiveness.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonology consultation, visit date 2020-12-04. Received and filed 2020-12-14.

Reason for referral: possible asthma.

This 35-year-old teacher reports six months of intermittent dyspnea, chest tightness and expiratory wheeze, chiefly nocturnal and with exertion. Relief with albuterol, which her primary care physician started in September. She has type 2 diabetes on metformin. Never smoker, no occupational or animal exposures. Mother with asthma.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily; albuterol MDI as needed.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Exam: RR 16, HR 72, BP 125/78, SpO2 98% on room air. Comfortable at rest. No nasal polyps. Chest clear to auscultation without wheeze at rest. Heart regular. No clubbing or edema.

Studies: Spirometry within normal limits, FEV1 2.8 L (80% of predicted) and FVC 3.5 L (85% of predicted). Methacholine challenge produced a 20% drop in FEV1 at 8 mg/mL.

Impression: Asthma. Symptoms with nocturnal waking more than weekly warrant a controller.

Recommendations:
1. Start fluticasone/salmeterol 100/50 mcg, one inhalation twice daily. Rinse and spit after each dose.
2. Continue albuterol as needed.
3. Return to pulmonology in about 3 months.

Thank you for this referral. Allergies: NKDA.

events.reason: Diabetes follow-up; review of pulmonology consult

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u diabetes and new asthma dx.

Pulm letter reviewed: normal spirometry, positive methacholine at 8 mg/mL, started fluticasone/salmeterol 100/50 BID. She has been using it faithfully for about 7 weeks. Night waking down to maybe once in two weeks. Albuterol a couple of times a week, mostly on cold mornings walking in from the parking lot. Rinsing after doses.

Diabetes: no lows, metformin twice a day. Back in the classroom part time and snacking less than when she was home.

Exam: no distress. Chest clear, no wheeze. Heart regular. Feet without lesions.

Assessment
- Asthma, newly diagnosed, improving on controller. Continue. Pulm f/u already booked for March.
- T2DM: A1c and CMP today.

Follow up in about 4 months for her physical.

medications.drug: omeprazole 20 MG Delayed Release Oral Capsule
medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth daily, 30 minutes before breakfast

reports.text: Pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry with good effort. FEV1/FVC mildly reduced with a concave expiratory limb. After albuterol, no significant change in FEV1 or FVC.
reports.conclusion: Mild obstructive defect without significant bronchodilator response.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonology follow-up, visit date 2021-03-17. Received 2021-03-29.

Seen about three months after her first visit for asthma. Since then breathlessness at night has crept back, and she has a persistent cough that is worse when she lies flat. She also describes chest burning after meals. She is reaching for albuterol more often and getting less from it. No recent colds, no new exposures at home or school.

Current medications: fluticasone/salmeterol 100/50 mcg twice daily, albuterol as needed, metformin 1000 mg twice daily.
Allergies: none known.

Exam: BMI 27. Mild end-expiratory wheeze both bases. Peak flow today 15% under her personal best. No stridor.

Data: CBC normal. Spirometry now shows mild obstruction, without a meaningful response to bronchodilator. We did not do esophageal pH testing.

Impression:
1. Asthma, not well controlled lately, with reflux as a likely contributor to the nocturnal cough and wheeze.
2. Gastroesophageal reflux disease, clinical diagnosis.

Plan:
- Omeprazole 20 mg every morning before breakfast.
- Head of bed raised, no food within 3 hours of bedtime.
- Continue fluticasone/salmeterol at current dose and albuterol as needed; inhaler technique reviewed.
- Return in 6 months or sooner if symptoms do not settle.

documents.title: Vaccine card
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Teachers got moved up so I got both my covid shots at the pharmacy, March 13 and April 3. Attaching a picture of my card. Also the reflux pill the lung doctor started is helping a lot already, I'm coughing less at night.

documents.title: RE: Vaccine card
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Daisy, both doses are entered in your record now. Glad the cough is better!

procedures.procedure: Preventive visit, established patient, 18-39

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, before work.

Since last visit: pulm follow-up in March found mild obstruction and reflux; on omeprazole 20 every morning since. Says the night cough is mostly gone and she sleeps through. Albuterol maybe once a week. Heartburn gone unless she eats late.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, fluticasone/salmeterol 100/50 BID, albuterol prn, omeprazole 20 daily. NKDA.
COVID series completed in April.
PHQ-2 zero.

Exam: well. BMI around 27. HEENT normal, no thrush. Neck no nodes. Heart RRR. Lungs clear, no wheezes. Abdomen soft, nontender epigastrium. Skin normal. Feet: intact sensation, good pulses, no skin breakdown.

A/P
- Asthma: controlled on current regimen.
- GERD: well controlled on omeprazole.
- T2DM: A1c, CMP, lipids, urine microalbumin. Eye exam due in August.
- Prevention: Pap due this year with GYN; she has an appointment in the fall. Flu shot in the fall.
- They are hoping to try for a pregnancy soon. Reviewed: tell us and OB right away when it happens so diabetes care can be coordinated early.

RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 6.8, steady. Lipids, metabolic panel and urine microalbumin normal. Message sent.

medications.sig: Taper: 4 tablets (40 mg) daily for 7 days, then 3 tablets daily for 7 days, then 2 tablets daily for 7 days, then 1 tablet daily for 7 days, then stop

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Same-day request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called, wheezy and coughing for about four days, using albuterol 4-5 times a day with short relief. No fever. Able to talk in full sentences on phone. Offered 11:20 today with PCP, accepted.

documents.title: Acute Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Asthma flare. Four or so days of wheeze, chest tightness and a dry cough, needing albuterol several times a day and waking twice a night. Setting up her classroom last week, lots of dust from boxes. No fever, no sore throat, no sick contacts that she knows of. Still on fluticasone/salmeterol twice daily.

Exam: mildly winded with talking but not in distress. Afebrile. Sat 96% on room air. Scattered expiratory wheezes both lung fields, fair air entry. No accessory muscle use. Heart regular, a little quick.

Assessment: asthma exacerbation, moderate, outpatient-manageable.

Plan:
- Prednisone taper, starting 40 mg daily, then stepping down by 10 mg each week, four weeks total. I went longer than a burst because she has needed albuterol this often for days; she knows it will push her sugars up.
- Albuterol every 4 hours while symptomatic, then back to as needed.
- Continue the controller.
- Check sugars once a day while on prednisone; call if fasting runs over 250.
- Return precautions reviewed: worse breathing, albuterol not lasting 2 hours, any trouble talking: ED.
- Nurse to call next week.

documents.title: Nurse follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt as planned. Breathing much better, on 30 mg week of taper. Albuterol once yesterday. Morning sugars 150s-180s, no symptoms. Reminded to finish the full taper. Will call if any return of wheeze.

medications.sig: Apply thinly to affected skin twice daily for 2 weeks

documents.title: Gynecology Office Note
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Gynecology office visit, date of service 2021-09-20. Copy sent to primary care on request; received 2021-11-10.

S: 36 y/o with asthma, type 2 diabetes, reflux. Seen by pulmonology this past year for asthma and reflux. Comes in with an itchy rash in both groin creases for two weeks. Noticed it got worse after switching to a new line of workout leggings. Has been on a prednisone taper from her PCP for the past month for an asthma flare.
Meds: fluticasone/salmeterol 100/50 BID, albuterol prn, metformin 1000 BID, omeprazole 20 daily, prednisone taper (finishing).
Allergies: NKDA.

O: Both inguinal folds with red, sharply demarcated plaques and scattered satellite papules and pustules at the edges. No inguinal nodes palpable. Remainder of skin exam unremarkable.

A: Cutaneous candidiasis of the inguinal folds, likely helped along by steroids, diabetes and occlusive synthetic fabric.

P: Clotrimazole 1% cream twice daily for two weeks. Keep the area dry, cotton underwear, loose clothing for exercise. Return if not cleared in two weeks. Cervical screening discussed; she prefers to schedule it separately.

documents.title: Big news
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I took a test this morning and it's positive! First appointment with OB is in 2 weeks. Do I keep taking metformin and my inhalers? Also the rash I had in my groin cleared up with the cream my gyn gave me, sorry I forgot to tell you about that visit.

documents.title: RE: Big news
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! Yes, keep taking metformin and both inhalers for now. Uncontrolled asthma is a bigger risk to the pregnancy than the inhalers are. OB will take the lead on diabetes in pregnancy and may change things. I'd like to see you in about a month to check your A1c and line things up with them. Glad the rash is gone; we'll ask your gynecologist to send that note.

procedures.procedure: Immunization administration

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine, inactivated, given IM left deltoid. Early pregnancy; confirmed inactivated vaccine appropriate. No reaction.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM
Immunization administration

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
About 10 weeks pregnant by her OB's dating. Some nausea in the mornings, managing with crackers, keeping fluids down. OB saw her in late October and wants her to stay on metformin 1000 BID and work with their diabetes educator on a pregnancy meal plan. Checking fingersticks four times a day now and the numbers have mostly been in range.

Asthma quiet since the prednisone in September. Reflux a little worse with the pregnancy, still on omeprazole.

Gyn note from September arrived last week: groin candidiasis, treated with clotrimazole. She says it's fully cleared.

Exam: well. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

Plan
- Diabetes in pregnancy: A1c and BMP today, results to OB. OB is managing during pregnancy; I'll stay in the loop.
- Asthma: continue controller and rescue.
- COVID booster today, she wants it before the holidays at school.
- Candidal rash resolved.

I'll see her after delivery unless something comes up.

documents.title: Inhaler refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting refill of fluticasone/salmeterol 100/50 diskus, last fill was from pulmonology with no refills left. Routed to PCP; approved x 3 refills. Pharmacy notified.

medications.sig: Swish 5 mL in the mouth and swallow four times daily for 10 days

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Acute Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 weeks pregnant, here for a week of sore throat and pain when she swallows. Has noticed a white film on her tongue that she can't brush off. No fever, no cough beyond baseline, no breathing trouble. No asthma flares since the fall. Has been on fluticasone/salmeterol twice a day for over a year now; admits she has gotten lazy about rinsing afterward.

Vitals all normal.

Exam: White plaques on the buccal mucosa and dorsum of the tongue, stuck on firmly; a tongue blade lifts a little and leaves a slightly bleeding base. Posterior pharynx mildly red, no exudate on tonsils. No cervical lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear both sides. Gravid abdomen appropriate for dates.

Assessment: oral candidiasis (thrush), related to inhaled steroid.

Plan:
- Nystatin suspension 5 mL swish and swallow four times a day for 10 days. Chose this over fluconazole because of the pregnancy.
- Rinse, gargle and spit after every controller dose; use a mirror and check the mouth weekly.
- If swallowing gets worse or she can't eat, call; would want to look further.
- OB updated by fax.

documents.title: Mouth update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Finished the nystatin yesterday. White stuff gone and swallowing is normal. I'm rinsing after the inhaler every time now, promise.

documents.title: RE: Mouth update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great to hear. Keep up the rinsing. Best of luck with these last weeks.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital emergency department, 2022-06-05. Faxed to primary care 2022-06-30 with the inpatient summary.

CC: seizure.

HPI: 37-year-old woman, one day after a vaginal delivery of her first baby following a long labor that needed oxytocin augmentation. Went home this morning. Husband says she had a generalized shaking episode on the couch lasting about a minute. Before that she had been queasy for hours and increasingly muddled, asking the same questions. She had no headache, no visual symptoms and no belly pain before the event. History of asthma, type 2 diabetes, reflux, recent oral thrush. Diabetes in this pregnancy was managed without insulin.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, fluticasone/salmeterol 100/50 BID, albuterol prn, omeprazole 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: T 37.1 C, BP 130/85, P 88, RR 16. Drowsy, postictal, rousable to voice and follows commands. No focal weakness, pupils equal and reactive, no clonus. Lungs clear. Fundus firm below umbilicus, lochia normal amount.

Labs: Na 122, K 4.2, Cl 88, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, glucose 140. Serum osmolality 260, urine osmolality 500.

MDM: Seizure with hypotonic hyponatremia, inappropriately concentrated urine, BP not elevated and no preceding headache or visual change. Picture fits water retention from oxytocin and IV fluids in labor. Given 3% saline 100 mL IV over 10 minutes, seizure precautions. OB consulted. Admitted to the medical floor with OB following.

Dispo: admitted.

conditions.label: History of gestational diabetes
conditions.note: as coded in the OB discharge summary

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 2022-06-05, discharged 2022-06-08. Received by primary care 2022-06-30.

Principal diagnosis: hyponatremia with generalized seizure, postpartum.
Other: type 2 diabetes; gestational diabetes in the recent pregnancy (per OB record); asthma; GERD.

Course: Arrived from the ED after a 3% saline bolus for a sodium of 122 and a seizure on postpartum day 1. Free water restricted to 1 liter a day. Sodium 126 at 6 hours, 129 at 24 hours, 133 at 48 hours and 135 on the morning of discharge, within safe correction limits. No further seizures. Mental status back to normal by the first evening. Metformin and inhalers continued. OB followed daily; postpartum course otherwise routine and she was able to breastfeed. Felt to be related to oxytocin and IV fluids during labor.

Discharge meds: unchanged from admission.
Follow-up: primary care in 1 week with a sodium check. OB postpartum visit as scheduled.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I had my baby on Saturday!! But the next day I had a seizure at home and had to go to the ER. They said my sodium was really low. I was admitted for 3 days and I'm home now and feel ok, just tired. They said to see you in a week to check my sodium.

documents.title: RE: Was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations, and I'm so sorry you went through that. Let's get you in Tuesday for a visit and a sodium level. We'll ask the hospital for the records. Until then keep following the fluid limit they gave you, and call 911 for any confusion or another seizure.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Requested ED and inpatient records from the hospital for 6/5-6/8 admission.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
10 days postpartum, brought the baby along. Per patient: delivered 6/4 after a long labor sped up with pitocin, discharged next morning, seized at home that afternoon, sodium very low, three days inpatient with salt solution and fluid restriction. Records requested, not here yet.

Now: no headaches, no confusion, no further episodes. Sleeping in pieces with a newborn. Drinking to thirst, no longer restricting. Breastfeeding. Mood good, PHQ-9 3. Asthma quiet. Sugars fine on metformin.

Exam: alert and oriented, conversational, no focal findings. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
- Hyponatremia, recovered: BMP today.
- Seizure: single event explained by acute sodium drop; no recurrence. Not driving until we see the level and she feels fully herself.
- T2DM: continue metformin, compatible with breastfeeding. A1c at the fall visit.
- Postpartum care with OB.

Will call with result.

documents.title: Sodium result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sodium 138, normal. Called patient, she was relieved. Hyponatremia resolved. No limit on fluids needed now.

documents.title: Hospital records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED and discharge summary from 6/5-6/8 now in chart. Matches her account. Discharge summary codes gestational diabetes for this pregnancy, which I've added as a history item; her type 2 diabetes remains the active diagnosis.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM
Immunization administration

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back at work two weeks, baby with grandma during the day. Breastfeeding in the mornings and evenings. Period came last week, first one since delivery.

DM: on metformin 1000 BID, sugars when she checks are 110s-130s fasting. Eats on the run.
Asthma: fine, albuterol rarely. Rinsing after the diskus, no thrush since spring.
Reflux: controlled.
No headaches or neuro symptoms since June.

Exam: no distress. Mouth clear. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Feet intact to monofilament, no lesions, DP pulses palpable.

Plan
- A1c, CMP, CBC, lipids, urine microalbumin.
- PCV20 today given asthma and diabetes; flu vaccine today.
- Eye exam overdue, gave her the optometry number again.
- RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Surprise
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Well this is a surprise but I'm pregnant again. OB knows. Same plan with the metformin?

documents.title: RE: Surprise
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! Yes, same plan unless OB changes it: metformin, both inhalers, omeprazole. Let's meet in January to check in on sugars and breathing.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
About 18 weeks. Anatomy scan next week. OB visits going smoothly so far, no insulin, staying on metformin twice daily. Fasting sugars in the 90s, after meals under 140 most days.

Asthma steady; one cold over the holidays, needed albuterol a few days and that was it. Reflux back a bit at night, propping up on pillows.

Exam: well. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Heart regular. Mouth clear.

Plan: A1c today and copy to OB. Continue everything. Next PCP visit after the baby comes.

documents.title: A1c
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 6.1. Faxed to OB.

documents.title: Optometry report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Diabetic eye exam, 2023-03-07. Patient is pregnant, second trimester. Acuity 20/20 both eyes with glasses. Pupils normal. Dilated exam: optic nerves healthy, maculae flat, no microaneurysms, hemorrhages or exudates in either eye. No diabetic retinopathy. Recheck 1 year, sooner if vision changes during pregnancy.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily for 3 months

reports.text: Bedside transabdominal ultrasound immediately postpartum for retained placenta. Uterus enlarged, consistent with the immediate postpartum state. Echogenic placental tissue persists at the fundal implantation site. The placental bed is irregular, with loss of the normal hypoechoic boundary and placental tissue extending into the myometrium. No free fluid in the abdomen.
reports.conclusion: Retained placental tissue with myometrial invasion, consistent with placenta accreta.

reports.text: Specimen: placental tissue and uterine curettings. Gross: multiple fragments of placental tissue and tan soft tissue. Microscopic: chorionic villi directly apposed to myometrial smooth muscle without intervening decidua.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Labor and delivery operating room, 2023-06-22. Copy received by primary care 2023-10-05.

Preoperative diagnosis: retained placenta with postpartum hemorrhage.
Postoperative diagnosis: placenta accreta.
Procedure: ultrasound-guided suction curettage of adherent placental tissue; placement of intrauterine balloon tamponade.
Anesthesia: epidural, already in place for labor.

Findings: Firm, well-contracted uterus. Adherent placental tissue at the fundus with no plane of separation on ultrasound, removed in fragments under ultrasound guidance until the cavity appeared clear. Brisk bleeding from the placental bed settled once the balloon was inflated.

Specimens: placental tissue and curettings to pathology.
Complications: none beyond the indication.
Condition: stable to recovery. No blood products given.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Admission 2023-06-22 to 2023-06-25. Faxed to primary care 2023-10-05 after a records request.

38-year-old G3P1 at 39 weeks with type 2 diabetes, asthma and reflux, admitted in active labor. Prenatal course uneventful. Labor progressed normally to a spontaneous vaginal birth of a healthy boy, 1- and 5-minute scores 8 and 9.

The placenta had not delivered at 30 minutes. Attempted manual extraction led to heavy vaginal bleeding that persisted despite fundal massage and oxytocin; the uterus remained firm and the cervix open. Bedside ultrasound showed an irregular placental bed with placental tissue invading the myometrium. She went to the OR for ultrasound-guided suction curettage and an intrauterine balloon, which stopped the bleeding. Uterus preserved. Pathology confirmed placenta accreta.

Hemoglobin 12.5 on admission and 10.2 after the hemorrhage. Not transfused. Balloon removed the next morning with no further bleeding. Vitals remained stable.

Discharge meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, fluticasone/salmeterol 100/50 twice daily, albuterol as needed, omeprazole 20 mg daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily for 3 months.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: OB in 2 weeks and at 6 weeks. Any future pregnancy is high risk and needs early OB planning given the accreta.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Postpartum Check
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seven weeks after the birth of her son on 6/22. Hospital never sent us anything, so this is her account: normal labor, but the placenta would not come out and she bled a lot when they tried. Went to the OR, they scraped out the placenta with an ultrasound and put a balloon in. Told it was placenta accreta. Did not need blood. Sent home on iron, which she is taking daily with some constipation.

Saw OB at 6 weeks, everything healing. Bleeding finished.

Tired, which she says is mostly the two kids under 15 months. Sleeping when they sleep. PHQ-9 4, denies low mood. Asthma fine. Sugars a little higher since delivery, fasting 120s-140s.

Exam: a little pale conjunctivae. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P
- Recent postpartum hemorrhage from placenta accreta, treated: CBC today. Continue iron to finish 3 months.
- T2DM: A1c and BMP. Continue metformin.
- Records: requesting the delivery admission records.
- Mood screen reassuring; reviewed signs of postpartum depression and how to reach us.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request to the hospital's medical records office for L&D admission 6/22-6/25/2023, including operative and pathology reports.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Daisy, your hemoglobin is 11.6, so it's coming back up nicely from the bleed. Keep taking the iron through September. A1c 6.4, a little better than before the pregnancy. No changes for now.

documents.title: Delivery records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: June L&D records arrived after our August request: discharge summary, operative report, pathology confirming accreta. Consistent with what she told me. Of note, they recommend early OB planning for any future pregnancy.

procedures.procedure: Immunization administration

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine left arm, 2023-24 COVID vaccine right arm. Breastfeeding, no contraindication. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Finished the iron in late September. More energy. Weaned the baby last month. Back to teaching full time.

DM: metformin both doses. Fasting 130s. Not much time for exercise; eating the kids' leftovers.
Asthma: controlled, albuterol a few times a month. Thrush none.
GERD: fine on omeprazole.

Exam: color better. Lungs clear throughout. Heart regular. Feet: sensation intact, no lesions.

A/P
- Anemia after hemorrhage: recheck CBC today, expect normal.
- T2DM: A1c, CMP, lipids, microalbumin. Talked about a realistic goal: 20 minute walk with the stroller 3 days a week.
- Eye exam due in March.
- RTC 4-5 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 12.7, back to normal. A1c 7.0, up a bit; she knows. Lipids and kidney labs normal. Will revisit at next visit.

documents.title: Pregnant
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi doctor, I'm pregnant again, about 5 weeks. I called my OB right away like the hospital said because of what happened last time. They're seeing me next week. Should I still take everything?

documents.title: RE: Pregnant
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations, and good call contacting OB first. Yes, continue metformin, the inhalers and omeprazole unless OB tells you otherwise. Let's see you in April.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
About 10 weeks. Seeing high-risk OB given the accreta last year; they have her on metformin, fingersticks four times daily, no insulin so far. Fasting 95-105.

Asthma: well controlled. Reflux: worse with nausea, using omeprazole daily.
No bleeding or cramping.

Exam: well. Lungs clear. Heart regular. BP normal.

Plan: A1c and BMP, copies to OB. Continue meds. See me after delivery.

documents.title: Prior authorization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Insurance changed its formulary for July; fluticasone/salmeterol 100/50 diskus now needs PA. Submitted with asthma diagnosis, prior trial of albuterol alone, current pregnancy. Approved for 12 months same day. Pharmacy notified, patient picking up.

events.reason: Induction of labor for gestational hypertension

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Labor and delivery admission 2024-10-21 to 2024-10-23. Received by primary care 2024-11-14.

39-year-old G4P2 at 37 weeks, with type 2 diabetes managed through the pregnancy without insulin (coded as gestational diabetes), asthma, reflux and a placenta accreta in 2023, admitted for induction because of gestational hypertension. Admission BP 145/95, HR 88, RR 16, afebrile. Fetal heart tracing reassuring.

After discussion she chose epidural analgesia. About 30 minutes after placement she became nauseated and lightheaded; BP 85/45, HR 110, SpO2 98% on room air. Fetal tracing stayed reassuring throughout. Treated as hypotension from the neuraxial block: left uterine displacement, 500 mL lactated Ringer's bolus and phenylephrine 100 mcg IV. BP 112/68 within 10 minutes, symptoms resolved.

Labor progressed to a vaginal delivery of a healthy infant later the same day. Given the history, the team was prepared for hemorrhage; the placenta delivered spontaneously and complete, with ordinary blood loss.

Postpartum BP 130s/80s without medication; 132/84 on discharge.

Discharge meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, fluticasone/salmeterol 100/50 twice daily, albuterol as needed, omeprazole 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: BP check with OB in 1 week; postpartum visit at 6 weeks.

documents.title: Delivery summary reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: October delivery summary in. Induced for gestational hypertension; epidural-related drop in BP treated quickly; uncomplicated vaginal birth and placenta. Postpartum visit with me in December to recheck BP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM
Immunization administration

documents.title: Postpartum Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seven weeks out from the October delivery. OB postpartum visit last week was fine; their BP check at 1 week was normal. No home BP cuff. No headaches, no swelling. Pumping at work.

Three kids now, oldest is two and a half. Husband is home in the afternoons. PHQ-9 2.

Meds unchanged: metformin, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol, omeprazole.

Exam: BP normal today. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
- Gestational hypertension: resolved, normal BP off all medication. Note for the future: her lifetime cardiovascular risk is higher after this and with diabetes; recheck BP every visit.
- Epidural hypotension: resolved at delivery.
- T2DM: A1c, CMP, CBC.
- Flu vaccine today; she skipped it in pregnancy.
- Physical in February.

reports.text: Liquid-based cervical cytology. Specimen adequate, transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

procedures.procedure: Preventive visit, established patient, 40-64

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Turned 40 last week. Fasting for labs.

Year in review: third baby born in October after induction for high blood pressure; BP normal since. No asthma flares needing steroids since 2021, uses albuterol maybe twice a month, more with colds from the classroom. Rinsing after the controller. Reflux quiet on omeprazole. Sugars drifting up, fasting 130-150, admits evening snacking after the kids go down.

She would rather do Pap here than make a separate GYN trip this year.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, fluticasone/salmeterol 100/50 BID, albuterol prn, omeprazole 20 daily. NKDA. Never smoker, occasional wine.

Exam: well. HEENT normal, mouth without plaques. Thyroid normal. Breasts: symmetric, no masses, no nipple discharge, no axillary nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze on forced expiration. Abdomen soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, co-test collected. Skin normal. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses palpable, nails fine.

A/P
- Health maintenance: Pap/HPV co-test today. Screening mammogram ordered, first one. Colon screening starts at 45.
- T2DM: A1c, CMP, lipids, microalbumin, CBC. If A1c is above 7, we'll talk about next steps.
- Asthma: controlled on current step.
- GERD: continue.
- Eye exam: due, she will book.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Daisy, A1c came back 7.4. Not alarming, but higher than we'd like. Kidneys, blood count, cholesterol and urine protein are fine. I'd like to give the evening-snack swap and some walking a real try for 3 months before we talk about adding a second medicine. Sound OK? Pap results take about a week.

documents.title: RE: Physical results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Yes that's fair. I'll stop the late night cereal. See you in May.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Your Pap and HPV test are both normal. Next one in 5 years.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammography with tomosynthesis. No prior studies for comparison. Scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcifications in either breast.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1, negative. Routine screening in 1 year.

documents.title: Mammogram
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Negative screening mammogram. Letter to patient; repeat yearly.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three-month recheck. Cut out the late snacks most nights; walking with the double stroller on weekends. Down a little on the scale. Fasting sugars 115-130.

Asthma: quiet. Still on the diskus twice daily.

Exam: lungs clear today. Heart regular. Feet fine.

Plan: A1c today. If under 7, stay the course. Eye exam booked for June. Back in September with flu shot.

documents.title: A1c
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 6.6. Nice turnaround. Message sent; no medication change.

documents.title: Optometry report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Annual diabetic eye evaluation, seen 2025-05-29. Best corrected acuity 20/20 both eyes. Dilated retinal exam normal in both eyes: no microaneurysms, dot-blot hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization. Assessment: diabetes without retinopathy. Next exam 12 months.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called re: missed visit yesterday. Pt apologized, first week of teacher in-service and she lost track. Rebooked for 9/24 at 3:45.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM
Immunization administration

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here after school. Sorry about August.

DM: summer was looser with the kids home; back to her routine now. Fasting 120s-140s. Metformin twice daily, no GI trouble.
Asthma: no night waking. Albuterol a couple of times since school started. Controller twice a day, rinsing.
GERD: fine.
Mood good, PHQ-2 1.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, fluticasone/salmeterol 100/50 BID, albuterol prn, omeprazole 20 daily. NKDA.

Exam: no distress. Oral mucosa clear. Lungs clear to auscultation, no wheeze. Heart regular, no murmur. No edema. Feet without lesions.

A/P
1. T2DM: A1c, BMP, lipids, urine microalbumin today.
2. Asthma: controlled; continue. Classroom colds are her usual trigger, so start albuterol early and call if she needs it more than every 4 hours.
3. GERD: continue omeprazole.
4. Flu and 2025-26 COVID vaccines given.
5. Mammogram due March.

RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Vaccine administration
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu 0.5 mL IM left deltoid; COVID 2025-26 IM right deltoid. VIS given. Waited 15 minutes, felt fine.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from yesterday: A1c 7.4, up again after the summer. Kidney function, cholesterol and urine protein normal. No changes today; at your January visit let's talk about whether to add a second diabetes medicine.

documents.title: ICU and Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: pulmonary critical care
documents.body:
Admitted 2025-10-06 (medical ICU), transferred to the floor 2025-10-08, discharged 2025-10-11. Sent to primary care 2026-01-21 in response to a records request.

History: 40-year-old teacher with asthma and GERD followed by pulmonology since 2020, plus type 2 diabetes. Three days of escalating dyspnea, wheeze and cough with no benefit from her usual albuterol.

Presentation: RR 28, HR 110, BP 135/85, SpO2 89% on room air. Using accessory muscles; diffuse expiratory wheezing. Initial arterial gas pH 7.35, PaCO2 45, PaO2 60, HCO3 24. Nebulized albuterol and ipratropium gave no improvement in work of breathing, and a repeat gas showed pH 7.32, PaCO2 50, PaO2 58.

Diagnosis: status asthmaticus with impending respiratory failure.

Course: Admitted to the ICU. IV methylprednisolone 125 mg, then 60 mg every 6 hours. Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV. Continuous nebulized albuterol. Started on BiPAP; arterial gas after 2 hours on BiPAP: pH 7.38, PaCO2 41, PaO2 78. Not intubated. Weaned off BiPAP on 10/7 and to the floor on 10/8. Steroids changed to oral prednisone. Wheeze cleared gradually and she was walking the halls on room air before discharge.

Discharge medications:
- Prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 more days
- Fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 mcg, one inhalation twice daily (increased from 100/50)
- Albuterol MDI as needed
- Metformin 1000 mg twice daily
- Omeprazole 20 mg daily
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Follow-up: pulmonology in 2 weeks. Primary care at her convenience.

documents.title: I was in the ICU
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted you to know I was in the hospital last week for my asthma. It got really bad and I ended up in the ICU on one of those breathing masks for a day. I'm home since Saturday. They put me on a stronger version of my inhaler and steroids for a few more days. I see the lung doctor next week. I'm ok, just wiped out.

documents.title: RE: I was in the ICU
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Daisy, I'm so glad you're home. Please keep the pulmonology visit, and use the new inhaler strength they gave you. Steroids can push your sugars up for a week or so, so check a few fasting readings. If breathing gets worse at all, go straight back in. We'll get the hospital records.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Requested discharge summary for October ICU admission from hospital HIM. They said 2-4 weeks.

documents.title: Records follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Still no ICU summary. Called HIM again, request was misrouted. Resubmitted.

documents.title: Hospital records filed
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Discharge summary for 10/6-10/11/2025 admission received and scanned. Routed to PCP inbox.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request: metformin 1000 mg #180. Last visit 9/2025. PCP approved 90 days; note to patient to book a diabetes visit.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can I get a refill on the omeprazole? Pharmacy said no refills left. Sorry I haven't been in, this year has been nuts. I'll call to schedule after school lets out.

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Sent a 90-day supply. Please do call the front desk to set up a visit, the doctor would like to see you.
